chapters.title: Chapter 191: Heading Out
paragraphs: Kaiden let out a sigh before rising from the water with Bastet still nestled in his arms. With a few exchanged glances and silent nods, the group knew what had to come next.
They changed clothes and called for the twins.
Moments later, Riven and Rae, their bodyguards who were known as the ’Creation & Destruction Twins’ in many prominent awakened circles, entered.
Riven’s expression was neutral. Rae, in contrast, had a lollipop in her mouth and looked like she’d just woken up from a nap.
"We’re heading out," Kaiden informed them. "I’d like you to secure transport."
Riven gave a nonchalant nod, knowing the protocol and what her duty entailed. "I’ll notify the higher-ups of our exit pattern."
"Let’s roll, bossman," Rae added, her voice muffled around her candy before she flicked it into her mouth with a loud crunch.
Within minutes, they were moving.

Their vehicle was one of the government’s hidden transport prototypes. It was artifact-enhanced, silent, shielded from tracking and most forms of magical or mana-based detection. It looked like a sleek, matte-black SUV from the outside, but its frame was reinforced with mana-threaded alloys, warding runes, and cloaking enchantments.

Riven took the driver’s seat, and her fingers soon began gliding across the control interface. Once they began moving, beside the vehicle, Rae ran. Not just jogging but running at full speed, keeping up with the transport without even breathing hard. Her powerful legs moved like pistons, her eyes scanning every shadow, every movement of wind or bird.

Within thirty minutes or so, the vehicle turned down a dirt road that didn’t exist on any maps, one that passed through an illusionary barrier and into a dense, mountainous forest where few dared tread.
As they approached their destination, a sprawling mansion nestled deep within a shrouded grove of stone and shadow, Rae’s eyes widened.
Her tan skin visibly paled.
"Wait..." she muttered, looking from the barely visible house to the road behind them. "This isn’t... this isn’t where I think it is, right?"

The tanned chick was practically vibrating now, her usual manic, chaotic energy cranked into full-blown hype mode. She tiptoed and squinted her eyes at the mansion, pupils dilated, a feral grin spreading across her face.
Before anyone could respond, Aria clapped her hands cheerfully with so much gusto that the seatbelt across her lap barely kept her from bouncing in place.
"I can’t believe it~! I’m getting to see Mom, Lux, and Damian so soon after being separated!" she said with sparkly eyes, radiating pure joy.
Rae’s head whipped toward Kaiden, eyes wide with gleaming excitement.
"... Kaiden!" Her voice was low but electric, like a fuse about to go off.
Kaiden only smirked, amused by how the girl was outright tweaking at the prospect of visiting this place. He didn’t know she harbored such strong feelings about ’them.’

In the next moment, the subtle hum of artifact-powered wards triggered around the perimeter, followed by a ripple in the air as a black-clad squad phased into visibility, surrounding the vehicle with cold professionalism.

Every one of them wore tactical bodysuits lined with reactive armor plating, matte-black and trimmed with lines of glowing crimson circuitry. Each soldier carried high-tier mana weapons slung across their backs and artifact-tech visors obscuring their faces.
No insignias. No visible rank markings. Pure shadow unit.

Immediately, Riven and Rae moved into bodyguard mode, sensing the immense threat these guards could pose to their charges. Riven snapped open a compact barrier drone from her utility belt while Rae simply clapped her hands together, always eager to crack some heads wide open.
But then, Kaiden lifted a hand.
"Stand down."
The twins paused, then stepped back into neutral positions. Though Rae still bounced slightly on her heels like a spring wound too tight.
One of the armored soldiers stepped forward, clearly the leader. His helm retracted just enough to reveal a chiseled jaw and silver eyes, sharp and unreadable.
"Kaiden Grey. I’m under strict orders not to let anyone pass beyond this point unless they are aligned with the Ashborn family... and only with explicit permission from the heads of house."
Kaiden’s smirk faded into a thin, bitter line. His jaw clenched slightly.
’Of course. I’m disowned, after all.’’
He was reaching into his pocket for his phone, ready to call her, when the soldier’s comm flared to life.
The air turned cold.
"Let them in."
The voice was mechanical, sharp, and unmistakably female. Calm in a way that carried command without needing to raise in volume.
Rae froze, pupils shrinking.
But then, in the next moment, she practically launched forward like a human rocket toward the gates, vibrating with pure starstruck energy, eager to meet her idol, the one and only Vespera Ashborn.
But then the voice came again.
"Keep the government hounds away from my home."
The comm went dead with a soft click.
Rae skidded to a halt just before the mansion’s massive garden gates, her eyes wide and sparkling, heart hammering like a war drum.

"Oh my god, that was Vespera for sure... She just looked down on me like I was some filthy mutt about to piss on her porch... And I—" Rae clutched her chest, the manic glint in her eyes stronger than ever. "—I didn’t know I was like this! Why does my heart feel so full all of a sudden?!"
Riven let out a slow, tired sigh, the kind that came from a sibling who had clearly seen this madness one too many times.

She de-summoned her floating defensive drone with a flick of her wrist. Her generous chest rose and fell beneath the reinforced chestplate she wore as she strode forward and firmly grabbed Rae by the arm.
"Hopeless. Utterly hopeless..." Riven muttered, then turned her gaze toward Kaiden. "We’ll stay here. Signal me if things go sideways. But..."
Kaiden nodded with understanding. "I know. Don’t expect miracles. I appreciate it, Riven."
The guards standing nearby made no move to stop them now. Kaiden stepped past the open gates, his Valkyries and felinid lover flanking him as they moved into the estate’s outer garden.
The transition was surreal.
One step from a random location in the greenery into otherworldly tranquility.

The garden was impossibly pristine, its stone paths lined with glowing crystal-bloom flowers, carefully curated brush, and whispering willow trees. The air was rich with floral perfume and distant mana signatures, while the sound of running water guided them deeper into the heart of the estate.
But then...
Something shifted.
A tremble in the air.
Kaiden paused, eyes narrowing as he sensed something.
Then, just ahead, peeking from behind a tall, carved pillar of white marble, a girl’s face became visible.

She looked barely older than a teen, though anyone who knew her wouldn’t be fooled by appearances. Long, inky black twin-tails draped past her waist. Her skin was pale like porcelain, smooth and flawless.
But it was her eyes that told the real story of what was going on in that head of hers.
Crimson red and wide with disbelief.

They shimmered violently with emotion, the edges trembling with unspoken memory and longing. Her legs visibly shook, and she reached out toward Kaiden with trembling fingers. For a second, she looked like she might collapse entirely.
Her lips parted, but no sound came.
Kaiden stopped in the center of the stone path, his gaze softening at the sight of the girl.
A faint smile curved his lips.
"Long time no see, Alice."

And I—" Rae clutched her chest, the manic glint in her eyes stronger than ever.
"—I didn’t know I was like this!
Why does my heart feel so full all of a sudden?!"
Riven let out a slow, tired sigh, the kind that came from a sibling who had clearly seen this madness one too many times.
She de-summoned her floating defensive drone with a flick of her wrist.
Her generous chest rose and fell beneath the reinforced chestplate she wore as she strode forward and firmly grabbed Rae by the arm.
"Hopeless.
Utterly hopeless..." Riven muttered, then turned her gaze toward Kaiden.
"We’ll stay here.
Signal me if things go sideways.
But..."
Kaiden nodded with understanding.
"I know.
Don’t expect miracles.
I appreciate it, Riven."
The guards standing nearby made no move to stop them now.
Kaiden stepped past the open gates, his Valkyries and felinid lover flanking him as they moved into the estate’s outer garden.
The transition was surreal.
One step from a random location in the greenery into otherworldly tranquility.
The garden was impossibly pristine, its stone paths lined with glowing crystal-bloom flowers, carefully curated brush, and whispering willow trees.
The air was rich with floral perfume and distant mana signatures, while the sound of running water guided them deeper into the heart of the estate.
But then...
Something shifted.
A tremble in the air.
Kaiden paused, eyes narrowing as he sensed something.
Then, just ahead, peeking from behind a tall, carved pillar of white marble, a girl’s face became visible.
She looked barely older than a teen, though anyone who knew her wouldn’t be fooled by appearances.
Long, inky black twin-tails draped past her waist.
Her skin was pale like porcelain, smooth and flawless.
But it was her eyes that told the real story of what was going on in that head of hers.
Crimson red and wide with disbelief.
They shimmered violently with emotion, the edges trembling with unspoken memory and longing.
Her legs visibly shook, and she reached out toward Kaiden with trembling fingers.
For a second, she looked like she might collapse entirely.
Her lips parted, but no sound came.
Kaiden stopped in the center of the stone path, his gaze softening at the sight of the girl.
A faint smile curved his lips.
"Long time no see, Alice."

chapters.title: Chapter 192: Long Time No See
paragraphs: Kaiden stopped in the center of the stone path, his gaze softening at the sight of the girl.
A faint smile curved his lips.
"Long time no see, Alice."
The twin-tailed girl audibly gasped with both delicate hands of hers shooting up to cover her mouth as if Kaiden had just confessed to a horrible crime instead of merely greeting her.
Her crimson eyes trembled harder than ever, shimmering with a mad cocktail of affection, obsession, and deranged glee. The moment hung still... until it shattered.
She took in a breath that sounded far too hungry for air.
"Big brother... called my name...!" she whispered, and then...

Her knees buckled. She clutched the pillar as if it were the only thing keeping her from fainting, her twin-tails flipping upward dramatically as her entire body twitched like she’d just received divine enlightenment. A high-pitched giggle broke from her throat, one that quickly devolved into a squealing whine as her emotions overloaded like a broken circuit board.
The Valkyries stood behind Kaiden, watching.
Luna tilted her head. "Uh..."
Aria leaned over to her, whispering. "And I thought I might be just a tiny bit unstable from time to time..."
Nyx just giggled, finding the sight adorable.
Kaiden, meanwhile, let out a chuckle of his own, shaking his head.
"You’re not gonna come give your big brother a hug?" he asked, parting his arms wide apart.
The effect was instant.
Alice jolted as if she had suddenly been electrocuted, every ounce of hesitation melting into one singular thought.

With a crazed expression, she shattered the marble pillar in front of her into a storm of white debris, sending shards flying as if they were glitter from a grenade. Next, a burst of radiant light magic enveloped her body, igniting with a pop as her form vanished in a golden flash...
And reappeared right in front of Kaiden a heartbeat later.
*WHAM!*

She tackled him with the force of a magical freight train, slamming him to the stone path with such wild strength that his breath flooded out on impact. His head hit the grass just off the path, eyes blinking up at the sky as his younger sister latched onto his chest as if she was currently busy cosplaying a heat-seeking missile.
"KaiKaiKaiKaiKaiKaiKaiKaiKai!!"

Her voice was a rapid-fire mantra of pure madness, her face nuzzling into his chest, arms squeezing tightly around his torso as she buried her entire existence into the warmth of her beloved big brother.

Kaiden wheezed, not just out of pain but also from the sheer disbelief at how freakishly strong she’d gotten. They hadn’t seen each other since he left for college years ago, and in that time, his sister was most certainly not slacking from grinding stats.

"Easy, Alice... you’re a... very big girl now..." he groaned, managing a weak chuckle even as she continued chanting his name and rubbing her cheek against his chest while wrestling the breath out of him.

Her twin-tails flopped back and forth with each nuzzle, and though her eyes were hidden from his sight, her delighted, muffled giggling echoed off the marble ruins around them. It sounded a lot like how the girls imagined the laughter of an unhinged cupid to be.
All three Valkyries looked at each other.
No words were exchanged. No signals. Just a long, silent glance between them—Aria’s eyes flicking from Luna to Nyx, Luna’s lips twitching with realization, Nyx giving a confident nod.
And in that instant, they knew.
This was her.
The Original Fangirl.

The one the system had credited Kaiden with the moment it first activated, the mysterious "foundational viewer" who somehow, impossibly, followed him before he’d even uploaded a single video. They’d all been wondering who the hell it was supposed to be, and honestly... they didn’t have a single doubt anymore.
This unhinged, crimson-eyed missile of obsession practically had "#1 FAN" carved into her soul.
Luna let out a sigh, one that was a bit confused on whether it should just be amused or concerned as well. "Yup. That’s her. The little sis has been the OG all along."
As if on cue, Alice let out another delighted squeal, her hands reaching for Kaiden’s lush black hair with obsessive energy as she chanted his name without even pausing to take a breath.
The Valkyries all stepped back to give the little sister space. Not out of mere politeness, but also self-preservation.

And yet, the girl’s rather concerning attitude didn’t bother her big brother one bit as he just chuckled, rubbing her back and petting her head, perfectly at ease with being the recipient of her madness.
"You took so long to greet me," Kaiden spoke up suddenly. "I was starting to wonder... Are you ashamed of your brother now? Because of the career path he’d chosen for himself?"
The effect was instantaneous and nuclear. As things often were when it came to Alice Ashborn.
"WHAT!?"

Her head launched upright, her eyes wide and horrified, pupils shrinking to tiny little dots. Her mouth opened in a shocked, horrified gasp before she began violently shaking her head left and right, side to side, fast enough to generate wind pressure.
"No-no-no-no-no-no-no-no!"
Her twin-tails became a blur behind her, swiping the air like helicopter blades about to summon a hailstorm.
"I would NEVER! I could NEVER! How CAN you even-!!"

Her voice cracked under the weight of her dismay. She grabbed his shirt in a panic with tears of distress forming in her eyes, looking like she was two seconds away from begging for forgiveness over an accusation he clearly didn’t mean seriously.
Kaiden chuckled again and slowly reached up, placing one hand gently against her cheek.

The moment his palm made contact, her body went dead still, ceasing her head’s fervent back and forth shaking. Not because of any strength he exerted, but because she was afraid that moving too fervently might somehow hurt him. Even her breath seemed to pause mid-inhale.
She blinked down at him, mouth agape, eyes shimmering.

chapters.title: Chapter 193: Never!
paragraphs: "I’d never be ashamed to call myself your little sister!" she decreed, voice trembling, passionate, and so intense it could’ve melted steel.
"NEVER! Not even if you became a villain!"
She leaned further in, pressing her forehead against his, letting the girl stare into his eyes from less than an inch away as she declared:

"I’ll always be proud to call myself your little sister! Don’t you EVER dare assume otherwise! Even if the whole world turns against you, I’ll still be here. Just say the word and I’ll kill them all!"
Alice wasn’t finished. Her voice grew fevered, eyes blazing with fanaticism. "Awakened humans, monsters, criminals, citizens, fathers and mothers, children—"
Kaiden sighed and raised a hand, gently placing a finger against her lips.
"I got it, Alice."
The little sister went stock-still instantly upon his actions. Her heart skipped. Her eyes shimmered.
’He silenced me... just like that...’
Internally, she squealed hard enough to rupture a dimension. Only her big brother could tell her to shut up and somehow make her adore him even more for it.
Alice let out a long, happy sigh and lowered her head to his chest, cheek pressed softly against his chest to dreamily examine the rise and fall of his breathing.

Her own breathing, once erratic and obsessed, calmed. For the first time since Kaiden’s arrival, she simply... rested. But soon, she spoke up with a low, fragile whisper. "... The reason I didn’t run to you right away was because... I thought seeing me might make you sad."
Kaiden’s eyes widened, caught off guard at the revelation. "Sad? Why would-?"
"I know you hate the Ashborn family, and I’m part of it. Same blood. Same name. I thought... if you saw me, you’d think of them. Of what they did. That it would hurt."
She shut her eyes tightly, voice trembling. "That’s why I never visited you at college... Even though I wanted to. Every single day... Every single hour... Minute... Second..."
Kaiden’s expression darkened.
"Alice... How could I hate you? That’s impossible."
She lifted her gaze again, blinking rapidly as if she didn’t dare believe what she’d heard.

"I hated them," Kaiden explained. "The way they looked down on me. The way Father treated me as if I was nothing but a stain on the bloodline. The way our siblings mocked me for being non-awakened..."
He reached up and gently cupped the back of her head.
"But not once—not once—did I ever think of you like that."
Her lips trembled. Her eyes glistened.
"I hate them..." she muttered, voice shaking with venomous grief. "I hate them more than anything. They deserve to suffer. They deserve to die for what they did to you."
Her palms curled into fists against his chest. "I tried... I tried to destroy them. After you left, I trained harder than anyone. I broke myself a thousand times and pieced myself together again."
Her teeth clenched. "But I couldn’t beat them... I couldn’t protect you. I’m a failure."
Kaiden stared at her for a long moment, then, suddenly, chuckled softly.
"Alice. You’re literally the last person on this planet who gets to call herself a failure."
Before she could argue, he shifted to stand. "C’mon. Let’s go greet Mother."
But Alice didn’t move from her spot.
Instead, like some overzealous monkey with a one-person tree, she clung. Her arms wrapped around his neck, her legs around his waist, her face pressed right back to his chest with stubborn resolve.
"I’m not letting go..."
"Ever again."
Kaiden sighed with a resigned smile and braced her weight with both arms.
Alice continued clinging like an adorable, psychotic little backpack.
But then, she sniffed.
*Sniff sniff.*
Her brow furrowed. She lifted her chin to get a better sense of the horrible stench her nostrils had picked up.
*Sniff-sniff-sniff.*
Suddenly, her nose wrinkled as if she’d just inhaled the scent of a carton of milk left open under the sun... ten years ago.
Her expression twisted with disgust. "What is that stench...?"
She craned her head around from her big brother’s embrace, and, at long last, spotted the culprits.
Four of them.
Luna, with wild purple hair and a little grin, directed right at Alice.
Aria, with a supermodel’s body, a soft, mature smile, and curves that could probably collapse nations.
Nyx, whose colossal tits might have had its own gravitational field and whose excitement at watching the scene unfold made Alice’s eyebrow twitch with contained violence.
And then Bastet... Bronzed skin, golden eyes, and a feline grace that screamed exotic. She even had the gall to look around so lazily, so nonchalantly, as if it were she who owned the garden.
Alice’s eyes twitched.
No. It was her very soul that twitched.
She slowly turned her head back toward Kaiden, her voice now dangerously high-pitched and sweet.
"...Big brother~?"
"Hmm?"

"Do we have to bring them?" she asked, fluttering her lashes, trying her best puppy-dog impersonation. "Can’t they wait here in the garden...? We have a kennel somewhere around here... They can stay there while you come inside..."
Silence.
Kaiden’s expression darkened instantly. His brows furrowed, eyes sharpening into blades.
"Alice."
That one word dropped onto the girl as if it were a hammer. She stiffened.
"You know how important these four women are to me. Every single one."
His voice wasn’t loud, but it carried that weight. That pressure that shut down any argument with pure, unshakable conviction.
"So, unless you want to get reprimanded by me seriously for the first time in your life, you’re going to treat them with the same respect you treat me. Understood?"
Alice gulped. Her whole body flinched. She didn’t like the tone her ears were picking up one bit. "Y-yes, big brother..."

Still clinging, still monkey-mode, she nodded obediently. But as Kaiden turned back toward the group, she slowly tilted her head to the side and stared right through the girls as if they were invisible.
Not a word. Not a wave. Not a blink. Just pure, icy, tactical non-acknowledgment.
And with that, Kaiden led the way deeper into Ashborn Manor.

chapters.title: Chapter 194: Into the Ashborn Residence
paragraphs: As Kaiden stepped through the grand archway of Ashborn Manor, the heavy doors groaned open, revealing the vast interior beyond.
The manor’s entrance hall was a spectacle of nothing but pure pride and power.
Vaulted ceilings stretched high above, painted with gold-trimmed murals of the Ashborn bloodline’s victories and the achievements of their high-tier guild, New Dawn.
The floor was an immaculate black marble, so polished it reflected the entire party like a mirror. Twin staircases curved upward, framing the main corridor that led deeper into the estate.

Lining the sides of the hall stood a formation of maids in crisp black and white uniforms, all standing straight-backed in a line. Their postures were flawless, eyes lowered, but not a single one bowed to Kaiden as they should to a direct line heir of the family.
Not a single one greeted him properly.
They bowed to him as if he were any other guest the Ashborn family decided to entertain in their home.
It didn’t matter that he was the oldest male child of the Ashborn family. Not after being disowned.

Alice’s arms tightened protectively around him, her gaze sharpening as she caught the coldness in the air. If her body language could scream, it would’ve threatened the maids and their whole lineage with brutal execution.
Then the atmosphere shifted.
From the upper staircase, three new figures emerged.
Descending with predatory elegance came the rest of the Ashborn siblings.
Twin brothers flanked a tall, imperious woman at the center; with each step they took, they oozed disdain.

The two men were mirror images of each other, tall and sharp-featured. Both wore dark formal combat robes lined with crimson, their lean frames made for speed and grace rather than brute power. They moved with the precision of hunters. Their eyes were red, and their hair was pure black.
These were Calix and Cassian Ashborn, the family’s twin prodigies.

And between them walked Selena Ashborn, the firstborn child. Taller than even the twins, her presence alone could command the room. Her long black hair flowed over her crimson-decorated shoulders. Her expression was calm but icy. Her eyes, which were akin to twin rubies, locked on Kaiden, and her lips curled into a smirk of superiority.
Selena spoke first, her voice a sharp, venomous blade. "Well, well, well. The generational failure returns."
Cassian snorted. "I simply can’t believe that Mother allowed you to enter after what you’d done."
Calix added with a nod, "The stench of a loser alone is proof enough he doesn’t belong in these halls. And look at what he’s brought. Four whores and a parasite hanging off his neck."
Alice’s body flinched. A low crack echoed in the hall as Alice slammed her heel into the marble floor hard enough to fracture it.
Her glare turned murderous, fangs bared. Alice’s body burned with fury, but before she could lunge, a hand settled on her shoulder.
She gasped.
Not from the touch, but from the impossibility of it.
’Impossible...!’
Because the pressure that suddenly blanketed the hall did not come from the twins.
It came from him.

Kaiden’s aura shifted in an instant, the gentle warmth she once knew drowned beneath a maelstrom of raw malice. His once-calm expression darkened into something terrifyingly still. The eye of a storm right before the world is torn apart.
His eyes changed.
No longer the simple red of an Ashborn outcast.

Now, they swirled, a violent, chaotic storm of crimson and orange, twin infernos coiling in opposite directions within his gaze. The red bled with seething wrath, the orange pulsed with insatiable gluttony.
Alice’s thoughts swirled.
’Big brother...? You never stood up to them before... You never fought back... You always endured. But now...’
This wasn’t the Kaiden who smiled gently through cruelty. This wasn’t the powerless man who let others hurt him. This was someone new.
Someone with power. With conviction. With the desire—no, the will—to protect himself and those he loved.
But before Kaiden could even open his mouth...
The world changed.
The light in the hall vanished.
Shadows didn’t slither in.
They outright exploded forth in all directions.

Like black ink bleeding into every corner of existence, they flooded down from the ceiling, across the walls, and up from beneath the marble floor, devouring all light, all warmth, all sense of safety.
The grand murals? Gone. The polished floor? Replaced by a churning abyss of shadow. The chandeliers hanging overhead dimmed to flickering whispers before being consumed entirely.
Vespera had arrived.
But not like a human woman.
Like a curse.

Her presence alone warped the very air. Maids, who were highly trained elite servants used to enduring magical pressure, quaked. Their knees buckled. Some whimpered without meaning to. Their breaths came shallow, panicked, as if the shadows themselves reached into their lungs.

A chill rippled down Bastet’s spine, every primal instinct in her felinid blood screaming in alarm. Something apex had entered the space. Something that made the air feel thinner, tighter. Not even when she’d faced Grace and her two elite bodyguards had the pressure been this suffocating.
But this wasn’t just raw power being let loose.
Luna, Aria, and Nyx each reacted differently.

Luna crackled with unformed electricity. Aria’s eyes gleamed silver as she stepped protectively closer to Kaiden. Nyx’s telekinesis shattered a nearby vase just from her reaction alone. She didn’t even notice.
But all of that—all of that—was nothing compared to what Calix, Cassian, and Selena experienced.
Their bodies shuddered.

Veins bulged across their foreheads and necks as their mana roared with all their might just to keep them upright. Sweat poured down their brows. Their red eyes widened. Not in surprise that something like this was happening to them. No. What they were experiencing was nothing but pure, unadulterated fear.
Cassian’s nose cracked with the strain. A stream of blood ran down his lip. Calix followed seconds later. His breath came out ragged. Panicked.
And Selena, who never trembled for anything, did now. Her poise cracked, knees buckling as she bit down on her lip hard enough to draw blood.
Then her voice came.
Low.
Bloody.
Impossible to resist.
"Who gave you permission to speak?"

sentences.text: As Kaiden stepped through the grand archway of Ashborn Manor, the heavy doors groaned open, revealing the vast interior beyond.
The manor’s entrance hall was a spectacle of nothing but pure pride and power.
Vaulted ceilings stretched high above, painted with gold-trimmed murals of the Ashborn bloodline’s victories and the achievements of their high-tier guild, New Dawn.
The floor was an immaculate black marble, so polished it reflected the entire party like a mirror.
Twin staircases curved upward, framing the main corridor that led deeper into the estate.
Lining the sides of the hall stood a formation of maids in crisp black and white uniforms, all standing straight-backed in a line.
Their postures were flawless, eyes lowered, but not a single one bowed to Kaiden as they should to a direct line heir of the family.
Not a single one greeted him properly.
They bowed to him as if he were any other guest the Ashborn family decided to entertain in their home.
It didn’t matter that he was the oldest male child of the Ashborn family.
Not after being disowned.
Alice’s arms tightened protectively around him, her gaze sharpening as she caught the coldness in the air.
If her body language could scream, it would’ve threatened the maids and their whole lineage with brutal execution.
Then the atmosphere shifted.
From the upper staircase, three new figures emerged.
Descending with predatory elegance came the rest of the Ashborn siblings.
Twin brothers flanked a tall, imperious woman at the center; with each step they took, they oozed disdain.
The two men were mirror images of each other, tall and sharp-featured.
Both wore dark formal combat robes lined with crimson, their lean frames made for speed and grace rather than brute power.
They moved with the precision of hunters.
Their eyes were red, and their hair was pure black.
These were Calix and Cassian Ashborn, the family’s twin prodigies.
And between them walked Selena Ashborn, the firstborn child.
Taller than even the twins, her presence alone could command the room.
Her long black hair flowed over her crimson-decorated shoulders.
Her expression was calm but icy.
Her eyes, which were akin to twin rubies, locked on Kaiden, and her lips curled into a smirk of superiority.
Selena spoke first, her voice a sharp, venomous blade.
"Well, well, well.
The generational failure returns."
Cassian snorted.
"I simply can’t believe that Mother allowed you to enter after what you’d done."
Calix added with a nod, "The stench of a loser alone is proof enough he doesn’t belong in these halls.
And look at what he’s brought.
Four whores and a parasite hanging off his neck."
Alice’s body flinched.
A low crack echoed in the hall as Alice slammed her heel into the marble floor hard enough to fracture it.
Her glare turned murderous, fangs bared.
Alice’s body burned with fury, but before she could lunge, a hand settled on her shoulder.
She gasped.
Not from the touch, but from the impossibility of it.
’Impossible...!’
Because the pressure that suddenly blanketed the hall did not come from the twins.
It came from him.
Kaiden’s aura shifted in an instant, the gentle warmth she once knew drowned beneath a maelstrom of raw malice.
His once-calm expression darkened into something terrifyingly still.
The eye of a storm right before the world is torn apart.
His eyes changed.
No longer the simple red of an Ashborn outcast.
Now, they swirled, a violent, chaotic storm of crimson and orange, twin infernos coiling in opposite directions within his gaze.
The red bled with seething wrath, the orange pulsed with insatiable gluttony.
Alice’s thoughts swirled.

You never stood up to them before...
You never fought back...
You always endured.
But now...’
This wasn’t the Kaiden who smiled gently through cruelty.
This wasn’t the powerless man who let others hurt him.
This was someone new.
Someone with power.
With conviction.
With the desire—no, the will—to protect himself and those he loved.
But before Kaiden could even open his mouth...
The world changed.
The light in the hall vanished.
Shadows didn’t slither in.
They outright exploded forth in all directions.

Like black ink bleeding into every corner of existence, they flooded down from the ceiling, across the walls, and up from beneath the marble floor, devouring all light, all warmth, all sense of safety.
The grand murals?
Gone.
The polished floor?
Replaced by a churning abyss of shadow.
The chandeliers hanging overhead dimmed to flickering whispers before being consumed entirely.

Like a curse.

chapters.title: Chapter 195: The Shadow Monarch
paragraphs: It didn’t echo through the hall like a normal sentence generated by a human’s vocal cords would.
No.
It burrowed into their minds. Into their bones. Her voice was weight itself. Her words were declarations.
An existential dread swept through the manor, thick enough to make even shadows seem too bright.
And still, she did not appear. No body. No silhouette. No face.
Just presence.
Just terror.
Just the knowledge that Vespera, Monarch of Shadows—the thing that should not be—was listening.
Was watching.
And she was angry.
Kaiden observed as the siblings who once made his life hell trembled beneath an invisible hand.

Selena’s knees refused to fully straighten. Cassian and Calix could barely stop their noses from leaking crimson. Their pride, the great Ashborn pride, meant nothing in the face of Vespera’s all-consuming rage.
For a brief moment, a storm swirled behind Kaiden’s eyes, his brain demanding he tell them never to speak like that to his family ever again.
But the fire died.
He exhaled through his nose. The fight in him from earlier was gone.
"You’re just as pathetic as I remembered..." With that, Kaiden turned, his eyes softer now as they found the four women behind him.
Kaiden gave them a quiet nod of reassurance, then gestured forward. Together, the six of them walked in unison, leaving the suffocating trio behind, still trapped under pressure they couldn’t escape.

They ascended the grand staircase. Their path led to a large set of ornate double doors, black and silver, carved with sigils that seemed to be illuminated by an oily sheen. The origin point. The eye of the storm.
Kaiden stepped forward and pushed.
The doors opened with a creak, and the world inside changed.

The shadows that had consumed the manor retreated. Coiling like smoke, they poured in from every crack, every crevice, funneling into a singular mass before slipping silently into the shadows at the feet of the woman lounging on one of two lush crimson sofas.
Vespera.
The Shadow Monarch.

Her legs were crossed elegantly, posture loose and languid, as if she hadn’t just bent the will of half a bloodline with a mere thought. She lifted a porcelain teacup to her lips and took a slow sip, her crimson eyes half-lidded, lazy, utterly indifferent to the chaos she’d just wrought.
Beside her, on the opposite sofa, sat a woman far more fragile in comparison.
Julia Levander.
Aria’s mother.

The illness still clung to her, but it was weaker now. Her face, once hollow and sunken, now bore color. Her cheeks held a soft blush. Her arms—though still slim—had gained the beginnings of strength. She wore a light shawl and a smile that trembled with emotion at the sight of her daughter and the man beside her. Clearly, Julia hadn’t felt the actions of Vespera just now. She was shielded, making her entirely unaware.
Behind them stood a tall woman in a maid’s uniform. Her presence was serene, but her posture was perfect. A loyal guardian.
Vespera’s handmaiden, Elizabeth.
The one who had raised and served the Monarch since childhood.
She offered Kaiden a warm, familiar nod, her eyes briefly lighting with fondness. "It’s been too long," she said softly, her voice full of sincerity.
Kaiden smiled. "Yeah... it has."
And like that, the oppressive air fully lifted.
The reunion had finally begun.
Without so much as a gesture of her fingers, Vespera’s mind touched the Awakened Platform’s interface, navigating to the Marketplace tab.
A pulse of mana shimmered in the space around them.

Then, out of the air itself, six elegant chairs materialized in sequence, crafted from a sleek obsidian alloy, high-grade artifacts bought directly from the marketplace. Their very presence radiated passive auras of comfort, posture support, and even mana stabilization.
Extra, through and through.
Vespera didn’t move.

It was her shadows themselves that acted, slithering across the floor, each lifting one of the new chairs and placing them in a perfect arc before her. As if arranged by an invisible butler staff trained in royal etiquette.
She didn’t so much as pause her tea sipping.
Kaiden exhaled a soft chuckle through his nose. Yeah. That was his mother. Extra didn’t even begin to give it justice.
He took his seat, which was right opposite Vespera’s. The chair adjusted subtly to his posture the moment he sat, using its embedded properties to the max.

Bastet settled into the one beside him, still a touch stiff and reserved from earlier. Nyx followed, crossing her legs and observing everything curiously, while Luna flopped into her chair without reservation, stretching her arms to experience what an artifact seat could provide her. Aria’s movement was the most elegant, gliding over and sitting down with bright eyes fixed on the woman across from her.
"Mom!" Aria beamed. "It’s only been a few days since I last saw you, yet you look so much better already! How have you been?"

Julia blinked as if not used to such brightness from her daughter, with whom she was reunited just recently, but smiled back with the motherly warmth that had long been missing from her features. "I... I’m still adjusting, Aria. Honestly, I was very shocked when Lady Vespera came to my hospital."
"Vespera."
A quiet silence followed after Vespera parted her lips to say her own name. One word. No emphasis. No sharpness.
And yet the air seemed to drop a degree.
Julia stiffened and nodded quickly. "R-right. Not Lady Vespera. Miss Vespera-"
"Vespera."
"... I was truly shocked to find Vespera in my ward. She told me my life could be in danger and that I was to come with her for my safety. Damian and Lux were sent to... um, the guest rooms-"
"Rooms."
Again, just one word. Just that voice. Like a scythe brushing across one’s neck, gently reminding you who ruled this domain.
Julia gulped, visibly rattled. "T-their... rooms. They’re in their rooms."
While the conversation continued, one person ignored it entirely.
Alice.
The sixth chair remained untouched.

Instead of taking it, she walked up to Kaiden, eyed it once with obvious distaste, then turned and plopped herself squarely into her big brother’s lap with zero shame whatsoever. She wriggled until she found the spot she liked, crossed her arms in front of her chest, and rested her head against his shoulder.
Kaiden wasn’t surprised, having become used to her antics.
The others, however, paused.
And for the first time since the pressure had vanished...
Vespera stopped sipping her tea.
Her head turned slowly, crimson eyes focusing on her daughter. The motion itself wasn’t fast, but it carried immense weight.
Her gaze, that had been so casual all this time, sharpened.

chapters.title: Chapter 196: Revealing Everything
paragraphs: Kaiden rested his hands on the comfy artifact seat’s armrest, his gaze observing the woman seated across from him. He could feel the tension spike.
Vespera didn’t speak.
She didn’t need to.

The air around her warped, the surface of her teacup vibrating as invisible pressure pulsed outward. This time, it was not violent, not filled with pure malicious intent like earlier, but deeply... maternal. In a terrifying way.
A monarch’s disapproval of her daughter’s actions.
Alice met her mother’s stare with a determined glare of her own, jaw clenched. And just like that, the staredown between mother and daughter began.
A single bead of sweat slid down her temple.
Still, she refused to move.
"I’m not getting off!" she decreed under her breath, arms crossed tighter. "It’s been years since I’ve gotten to sit in my big brother’s lap!"
Another wave of quiet pressure rippled out from Vespera’s still form.
Kaiden’s chair creaked.

"I missed him so much!" Alice gritted, now speaking louder as though defending herself in court. "And besides! It’s perfectly normal for a little sister to sit on her big brother’s lap! Our relationship is perfectly healthy sibling bonding!"
The shadows in the room grew a shade darker.
"I saw it! On the stream! The purple-haired one does it all the time!" Alice grimaced, gesturing blindly to her left.

"I’m your brother’s girlfriend, while you, little sis, is his full-bloo-" Luna replied, utterly amused. She’s never seen such an odd person before. But before she could finish, she was interrupted by a high-pitched, alarmed shout.
"S-shut up! It’s not like that, and that’s the end of the story!" Alice snapped, then turned back to her mother. "I refuse to get off! You’ll have to kill me!"
The room continued to tighten with unspoken gravity, a silent orchestra of judgment building toward a final crescendo.
Alice was trembling now, visibly sweaty, but her arms remained locked. "I... I didn’t even get to greet my big brother for years... I’m... just making up for lost time..."
Another pause.
The air was thick. Her shoulders shook, both from strain and nerves.
And then...
It stopped.
Just like that. No warning. No easing. No gradual fade.
The pressure vanished as if a switch had been flipped. The shadows returned to calm. The warmth of breathable air rushed back into the room.
Alice collapsed backward against Kaiden’s chest, sweat glistening along her forehead and collarbone. She was panting heavily, ragged breaths escaping her lips before she grinned triumphantly.
"I won..." she whispered.
Kaiden sighed through a small smile, brushing a few damp strands of hair from her cheek.
Across from them, Vespera sipped her tea once more, unbothered, as though the entire power play had never happened. But the faintest twitch at the corner of her mouth betrayed something else.
Something dangerously close to amusement.
A momentary lull took over the conversation. Kaiden shifted, letting Alice settle more comfortably against him. His gaze, however, never left the woman seated across from him.
He exhaled slowly, bracing himself to say what he had to.
"I’m... once again shamefully bothering you, to ask a favor."
Vespera didn’t reply.
She didn’t nod, didn’t blink.
She simply studied him.
Unmoving. Unblinking. Waiting.
The silence broke from another direction.
"M-may I say something?" Julia’s voice was meek, barely above a whisper, like a child speaking up in a place she knew she shouldn’t. She looked toward Vespera.
The Shadow Monarch’s crimson gaze shifted, slowly, deliberately turning to meet the woman’s eyes.
She gave a single nod.
Julia gulped and nodded back. "I... I just don’t understand... why does Kaiden hate asking for your help so much?"

She glanced toward Kaiden, then back to Vespera. "You have more than enough resources. And... from what I understand after spending time chatting with you and observing your actions, you don’t seem to mind helping your son at all."
Her lips trembled slightly, but her eyes were steady. "As a mother, I would be happy to give my daughter all the support she needs. So why... why does he resist you so much?"
Vespera didn’t answer. Instead, she remained silent in contemplation before she turned her head once again, this time back to Kaiden.
Waiting for his explanation.
Kaiden met her gaze for a long moment, his fingers slowly tapping against the chair’s armrest. He didn’t respond right away.
Soon, he sighed. Then he lifted his eyes and asked, "Is there any chance anyone might be able to listen in on this conversation?"
"No," Vespera replied instantly. "No one can."
But seeing his hesitation, she raised a hand and smacked two fingers together.
*Snap.*
The sound echoed with unnatural sharpness.
In an instant, blackness exploded outward. The windows darkened. The walls disappeared. The light was swallowed whole.
Shadows flooded the entire room, swallowing up every edge and corner in ominous silence.
The world was gone.
Only those in the room remained.
"Speak freely," Vespera said. Her voice was calm.
Hearing his mother’s statement, Kaiden’s eyes shifted, moving toward the three women seated beside him.
Luna.
Aria.
Nyx.
Each of them met his gaze.
He didn’t say a word.
He didn’t need to.
One by one, they nodded.
Supportive. Resolute. Unquestioning.
A silent pact reaffirmed.
Kaiden leaned back against his chair, exhaling slowly as he turned his eyes back to the woman across from him. Vespera didn’t pressure him. She simply waited.
He stared at her deep eyes for a long moment, collecting the tangled thoughts that had coiled in his chest for some time now.
Then he began.
"When I was a dejected college student, I had no hopes of living life the way I wanted. I was stuck. Forgotten. Studying my ass off to become just another cog in the machine."
He paused.
"That all changed, however.. .when I died."
Alice twisted on his lap, alarm flashing across her face.
She spun around completely, straddling his legs now as she grabbed the sides of his face, inspecting him with frantic intensity. "You died?! Where?! When?!"
Kaiden placed a calming hand on the hyperventilating girl’s head and ran his fingers through her dark hair.
"I’m fine now. Let me finish, Alice."
The twintailed teen pouted but paused her frantic search for mortal wounds on her big brother, instead folding her arms under her chest once again.
Seeing that she had calmed, Kaiden continued.
"I didn’t stay dead. Instead of falling into eternal slumber, I woke up once again. My broken body was healed. And there was a message staring at me, burned into my mind’s eye."
He lifted a hand and manifested the same message he saw back then.
A small, glowing screen flickered into existence above his palm.
[Welcome to the Pornstar System, host.]
Julia gasped sharply.
Alice blinked once, then twice, then made a sound like a balloon deflating in confusion.
Even Vespera—the unshakable Monarch of Shadows—raised an eyebrow.
Kaiden let the screen vanish with a flick of his hand.

"I’ve been doing my best to rank the system up, not just level myself. That’s why I’m getting stronger and stronger without needing to break through after hitting the usual cap of Level 25 like normal Awakened."
"I can grow both through combat and through the system itself. It’s a dual path where the paths themselves reinforce each other."

He spent the next few minutes detailing the last couple of months that had passed since gaining the system, its mechanics, how he fulfilled a hidden quest, and awakened his three girlfriends into Valkyries with immense potential. Once done, Kaiden turned his gaze to Julia.

I didn’t even get to greet my big brother for years...
I’m... just making up for lost time..."
Another pause.
The air was thick.
Her shoulders shook, both from strain and nerves.
And then...
It stopped.
Just like that.
No warning.
No easing.
No gradual fade.
The pressure vanished as if a switch had been flipped.
The shadows returned to calm.
The warmth of breathable air rushed back into the room.
Alice collapsed backward against Kaiden’s chest, sweat glistening along her forehead and collarbone.
She was panting heavily, ragged breaths escaping her lips before she grinned triumphantly.
"I won..." she whispered.
Kaiden sighed through a small smile, brushing a few damp strands of hair from her cheek.
Across from them, Vespera sipped her tea once more, unbothered, as though the entire power play had never happened.
But the faintest twitch at the corner of her mouth betrayed something else.
Something dangerously close to amusement.
A momentary lull took over the conversation.
Kaiden shifted, letting Alice settle more comfortably against him.
His gaze, however, never left the woman seated across from him.
He exhaled slowly, bracing himself to say what he had to.
"I’m... once again shamefully bothering you, to ask a favor."
Vespera didn’t reply.
She didn’t nod, didn’t blink.
She simply studied him.
Unmoving.
Unblinking.
Waiting.
The silence broke from another direction.
"M-may I say something?" Julia’s voice was meek, barely above a whisper, like a child speaking up in a place she knew she shouldn’t.
She looked toward Vespera.
The Shadow Monarch’s crimson gaze shifted, slowly, deliberately turning to meet the woman’s eyes.
She gave a single nod.
Julia gulped and nodded back.
I just don’t understand... why does Kaiden hate asking for your help so much?"
She glanced toward Kaiden, then back to Vespera.
"You have more than enough resources.
And... from what I understand after spending time chatting with you and observing your actions, you don’t seem to mind helping your son at all."
Her lips trembled slightly, but her eyes were steady.
"As a mother, I would be happy to give my daughter all the support she needs.
So why... why does he resist you so much?"
Vespera didn’t answer.
Instead, she remained silent in contemplation before she turned her head once again, this time back to Kaiden.
Waiting for his explanation.
Kaiden met her gaze for a long moment, his fingers slowly tapping against the chair’s armrest.
He didn’t respond right away.
Soon, he sighed.
Then he lifted his eyes and asked, "Is there any chance anyone might be able to listen in on this conversation?"
"No," Vespera replied instantly.
"No one can."
But seeing his hesitation, she raised a hand and smacked two fingers together.
*Snap.*
The sound echoed with unnatural sharpness.
In an instant, blackness exploded outward.
The windows darkened.
The walls disappeared.
The light was swallowed whole.
Shadows flooded the entire room, swallowing up every edge and corner in ominous silence.
The world was gone.
Only those in the room remained.
"Speak freely," Vespera said.
Her voice was calm.
Hearing his mother’s statement, Kaiden’s eyes shifted, moving toward the three women seated beside him.
Luna.
Aria.
Nyx.
Each of them met his gaze.
He didn’t say a word.
He didn’t need to.
One by one, they nodded.
Supportive.
Resolute.
Unquestioning.
A silent pact reaffirmed.
Kaiden leaned back against his chair, exhaling slowly as he turned his eyes back to the woman across from him.
Vespera didn’t pressure him.
She simply waited.
He stared at her deep eyes for a long moment, collecting the tangled thoughts that had coiled in his chest for some time now.
Then he began.
"When I was a dejected college student, I had no hopes of living life the way I wanted.
I was stuck.
Forgotten.
Studying my ass off to become just another cog in the machine."
He paused.
"That all changed, however.. .when I died."
Alice twisted on his lap, alarm flashing across her face.
She spun around completely, straddling his legs now as she grabbed the sides of his face, inspecting him with frantic intensity.
"You died?!
Where?!
When?!"
Kaiden placed a calming hand on the hyperventilating girl’s head and ran his fingers through her dark hair.
"I’m fine now.
Let me finish, Alice."
The twintailed teen pouted but paused her frantic search for mortal wounds on her big brother, instead folding her arms under her chest once again.
Seeing that she had calmed, Kaiden continued.
"I didn’t stay dead.
Instead of falling into eternal slumber, I woke up once again.
My broken body was healed.
And there was a message staring at me, burned into my mind’s eye."
He lifted a hand and manifested the same message he saw back then.
A small, glowing screen flickered into existence above his palm.
[Welcome to the Pornstar System, host.]
Julia gasped sharply.
Alice blinked once, then twice, then made a sound like a balloon deflating in confusion.
Even Vespera—the unshakable Monarch of Shadows—raised an eyebrow.
Kaiden let the screen vanish with a flick of his hand.
"I’ve been doing my best to rank the system up, not just level myself.
That’s why I’m getting stronger and stronger without needing to break through after hitting the usual cap of Level 25 like normal Awakened."
"I can grow both through combat and through the system itself.
It’s a dual path where the paths themselves reinforce each other."

He spent the next few minutes detailing the last couple of months that had passed since gaining the system, its mechanics, how he fulfilled a hidden quest, and awakened his three girlfriends into Valkyries with immense potential.
Once done, Kaiden turned his gaze to Julia.

chapters.title: Chapter 197: Explanation
paragraphs: "So to answer your question, Julia. The reason I don’t want to rely on my mother all the time doesn’t stem from some masculine insecurity. I know she’s stronger, more influential, more experienced, everything. She’s the full package, so to speak. If depending on Mother meant giving me and my girls a better shot at survival—at gaining immense power and freedom—I’d do it without hesitation."
Julia swallowed, listening with wide eyes.

"But as I explained, this system," Kaiden continued, "was created by the Heavenly Demon. A galactic terrorist who once rebelled against the universe itself. As his potential successor, what do you reckon he’d think if I ran crying to mommy to hide under her skirt every time something went wrong?"
"He would think you’re a failure, unworthy of the heritage," it was Vespera who replied in Julia’s stead. Her eyes gleamed with understanding now.
"Exactly. I’ve got to solve things myself. That’s what I believe. That’s the price of keeping this power. That’s why I only ask for your help when there’s no other way."
A heavy silence followed his words.
Julia gulped again. Hard.
Then nodded slowly. "I... I understand."
Vespera’s gaze had a tranquil sharpness to it as she asked:
"Then tell me, why are you here now?"
Kaiden didn’t hesitate this time around. He materialized the newest screen hovering above his palm.
[New System Quest: Fangirl Bottleneck]

[Quest Objective]: Demonstrate the ability to cultivate deep, lasting admiration from those who are merely intrigued. The Successor must display proficiency in converting fleeting interest into genuine, unwavering devotion.
He let the message linger for a few seconds before dismissing it with a swipe and turning to face his Valkyries.

"I haven’t shown this to any of you yet. It popped up a few hours ago. The bunker we were given by the government is perfect in most ways. Safe. Durable. Secure. The twins are also very capable bodyguards."

"But... There’s zero privacy in those walls. Microphones, cameras, artifacts... We can’t speak freely. That being said, I can navigate that. So can you girls. But when something extra happens—like a new quest—we need to think, talk, and plan together."
His eyes flicked to Vespera. "That’s why we came here. Not for protection. Not for backup. Just to speak in private."
For a few seconds, no one responded.
Then Alice perked up, her eyes lighting. "I could help! If fangirls are what you need, then I think-"
Kaiden silenced her.
"Alice. This isn’t something we will try to solve together. This is not a family homework assignment."
She blinked, brows drawing together in confusion and a heavily brewing taste of utter dislike.

Kaiden ignored the confused girl on his thighs and instead turned his gaze slowly to his Valkyries. "You three are different. The system recognizes you. You’re part of this, tied to me through awakening, combat, resonance, everything. You are my system-recognized partners in crime."
Then he looked at Julia and Alice in turn.
"But my family, or any of yours, isn’t. This system... if I let anyone outside the system influence it too much, the line gets blurry. I might not notice when I start leaning too hard."
He turned toward his mother, posture straightening
"And I know you’ve been protecting me from the shadows all this while."
Vespera didn’t deny it at all. Instead, she just kept observing her son mutely.
"But that also needs to stop," Kaiden said quietly.

"I appreciate it, Mother. I really do. But I can’t become the man I need to be if I always have a shadow of your caliber ready to clean up my messes for me. The Heavenly Demon isn’t looking for a pampered brat. He wants a worthy successor who can inherit his life’s work."
With finality, he concluded:
"This system—this chance I’ve been given—it doesn’t allow me to be carried. It requires that I earn everything."
A silence followed.
No one moved. Not even the shadows.
And then Vespera’s lips curved upwards.
It wasn’t a smile of mockery or amusement.
It was something quieter.
Pride.
Motherly pride for her son, who had grown into such a decisive, clear-eyed young man. A man who stood on the edge of a cosmic storm and chose to walk through it with open eyes and a steady hand.
She rose silently. Her eyes landed on Julia. "Can you stand?"
Julia nodded without hesitation, rising to her feet.
Then Vespera’s gaze turned to Alice.
The girl flinched, heart skipping a beat. Instinct screamed in her bones. Alarms rang in her mind like sirens.
"No!" she cried, reaching out and grabbing tightly onto Kaiden’s sleeve. "No!"
"Yes."
*SHHHRRKT!*
A hundred black tendrils surged out from Vespera’s shadow like coiled vipers.
In the blink of an eye, shadows enveloped Alice from every angle, grasping her wrists, her ankles, her waist, even curling around her throat.
"No! NO! I REFUSE TO LET GO!" she shrieked, writhing with all her might, tears stinging her wide, furious eyes. "I WON’T LEAVE MY BIG BROTHER’S SIDE EVER AGAIN! YOU’LL HAVE TO KILL ME, YOU HEAR ME?!"
Vespera’s calm, cold voice came down on the girl like falling dusk.
"You’re wrong."
Alice blinked.
"I have to kill you? Why?"
Her steps were slow as she approached the girl, but her presence was impossibly vast.
"I don’t."
She paused in front of the bound girl.
"To force me to either let you do as you want or kill you... You’d need to be strong enough to force my hand in the first place."
Vespera’s dark eyes narrowed.
"Only the wishes of the strong matter."
Alice’s mouth opened to scream again, but no sound came. The shadows tightened around her body, restricting her.
"And you are not strong enough to impose your will upon me."

The three Valkyries watched in stony silence the demonstration of the ’Ashborn-style parenting.’ Even Bastet narrowed her golden eyes at the sight, uncertain how to feel or think about what her eyes were showing her.
True to her word, Vespera didn’t have to kill Alice.
She simply peeled her off Kaiden, one inch at a time.
Alice kicked, thrashed, even bit the shadows, her wild limbs flailing at Kaiden.
Kaiden chuckled, shaking his head.
"I’ll come pay you a visit once this strategy meeting’s over."
The rage in Alice’s eyes cracked.
She froze mid-thrash. For a second, only the soft sound of her rapid breathing filled the room.
"Y-You mean it?" she breathed, her voice trembling.
Kaiden smiled gently. "Of course."
And for a moment, joy shone in Alice’s face. Pure, unfiltered joy. She stopped struggling, let the shadows lift her off the floor...
Then realization struck.
Wait.
If she stayed here, she could spend even more time with her beloved big brother. She could sit beside him, hold his arm, maybe even get petted again...
"NO! THAT’S NOT GOOD ENOUGH! LET ME GO! I’M STAYING!!!"
Too late.

The shadows pulled her back, whether she consented or not, getting vacuumed like a ghost, thrashing and whining, the sound of her muffled curses echoing into the distance as she was dragged from the room.
Vespera paused before leaving and turned halfway back.
"I’ll maintain the shadow field. Speak freely."
And with that, the door clicked softly shut behind them, leaving Kaiden and his Valkyries alone in a blackened world of absolute privacy.

chapters.title: Chapter 198: Damn
paragraphs: Nyx was the first to break the silence.
Then Luna followed, snorting with barely suppressed laughter before it spilled over.
"You’ve got one hell of a little sister," Nyx managed to mouth the words, wiping a tear from the corner of her eye.
Luna followed with a similar tone of voice. "Obsessed, clingy, loud, and terrifyingly committed. I can respect it. But also... damn. Just damn."
Kaiden rubbed the side of his head, sighing.

Across from them, Aria and Bastet didn’t laugh, but they weren’t exactly stone-faced either. Aria looked... unsure. She tilted her head, brows drawn in concern. Bastet, meanwhile, rested her chin on her fist, golden eyes narrowed in thoughtful amusement.
Then, Aria spoke.
"...Kai, you do know we’re not in the state of Alabama, right?"
Kaiden turned toward her, eyebrows lifting.
Aria didn’t back down. She didn’t look away. She met his gaze head-on, steady and unflinching, despite the clear nervousness flickering in her eyes.
He stared for a moment longer. Then sighed for a second time.
"It’s not like that. Alice is just..." He paused, searching for the right word. "Clingy. That’s all. She’s gonna grow out of it. For sure."
"She’s gonna grow out of it."
"For sure."
Nyx and Luna echoed in perfect sync, each word dripping with sarcasm.
Their matching looks said it all: You’re delusional.

Bastet finally chimed in as she tilted her head thoughtfully. "I don’t know much about human familial customs, but I’m pretty sure it’s not standard practice for the mother to have to pry her daughter off her son while she’s screeching about rather dying than being separated ever again."
Kaiden gave her a flat look.
"Thanks for the insight, Professor Bastet."
She gave him a feline grin. "I just voiced an innocent observation of mine, Master~"
He looked to the rest: Nyx’s amused smirk, Luna’s mischievous glint, Aria’s concerned brows, Bastet’s smug neutrality.
None of them looked ready to drop the subject.
They weren’t judging him. But they weren’t pretending this was normal either. Kaiden sighed the third time, heavier than ever before.
"Anyways... Let’s shift focus."
The girls laughed together at him running away, but didn’t press the matter any further.
A flicker of light shimmered into being above his palm.
The System window returned.
[New System Quest: Fangirl Bottleneck]
"This is what we’re dealing with now," Kaiden said.
"The system’s calling it a bottleneck..." Luna mused, stroking her chin in thought.

"Well, I mean, it clearly is a bottleneck. There’s no reason to put it more gently," Nyx added. "We have more than three times the needed views and income to reach rank 3, but we’re only one-tenth of the way to reach the fangirl requirement."
"But what else can we do?" Aria asked before continuing,

"Based on its own wording, which was ’the Successor must cultivate a following whose devotion stems from genuine connection and profound inspiration. Superficial engagement, while boosting views and income, does not translate into the deep admiration required for this metric.’ It clearly suggests that the fangirl metric is simply going to be slower to accumulate than the other two, no matter what we do."

Luna nodded in agreement. "You’re right, I believe. And we’ve already been trying to make Kai appeal to the horny sluts by doing variety content and also having things like your nurse RP focus on him."
*Clap!*
Nyx clapped her hands once, sharp and loud.
"Okay! Hear me out," she murmured with excited eyes.
"Instead of taking this side quest as us assuming that the system is saying we’re doing horribly... maybe we should take it as the system saying we’re just not doing enough."
Kaiden raised a brow. "Not enough?"

Nyx nodded. "Exactly! We’ve been dipping our toes into things, trying to be versatile, trying a little bit of everything. But the fangirl metric doesn’t reward ’a little of everything.’ It rewards obsession. We need to lean in, hard. Stop playing it safe and greedy."
Kaiden was a bit skeptical as he asked, "What do you suggest we do, then?"
Nyx leaned back in her chair, tapping a finger against her lips in exaggerated thought.
Silence hung for a beat.
Then her lips curled into a grin. Slow, confident, and utterly devilish.
"We need to rebrand."
"...Rebrand?" Aria asked, confused.
Luna didn’t speak. She just narrowed her eyes, her amusement gone, replaced with focused scrutiny. She knew Nyx well enough to recognize when her gears were turning fast.

Bastet remained silent but watchful. She didn’t know enough about human entertainment strategy to add to the conversation in any meaningful way for now, but she was clearly intrigued. After all, her master’s future growth potential was the topic being discussed before her.
Nyx nodded, "Rebrand, yes."
Her eyes were sharp now, the usual mischief replaced by genuine strategy. "Think back to that night at the sushi place. When Kaiden made us his Valkyries after the porn shoot."
Her gaze swept across the room, catching the gazes of the other two Valkyries.

"He told us his vision. That we were going to storm the world with content so bold, so captivating, so insane that no one would be able to ignore it. That we’d rise to the very top, not just in numbers, not just in influence, but in legacy. He wanted our faces etched into the damn mythos of this post-apocalypse world."

"And that’s perhaps just a tiny bit too ambitious. At least, for now. What we’re seeing now—what this bottleneck quest is telling us—is that there’s a consequence to trying to appeal to everyone at once."
Kaiden furrowed his brow, listening to his girlfriend intently.

"We’re spreading ourselves too thin," Nyx continued. "We’ve been trying to do it all. Cater to every fantasy, every viewer type, every demographic. Some content for women, some for men, some for the lonely, the horny, the curious, the bloodthirsty. And it’s worked. We dominate in views and income."
She lifted a finger.
"But that third metric? That devotion? It doesn’t care how wide we cast the net. It only cares about depth. About emotional entanglement. About fixation."
The air in the room shifted as her words sank in.

"So here’s what I’m proposing. We stop worrying about appealing to everyone on Planet Earth. We accept a drop in views and income. We narrow our focus. We build something targeted. Intimate. The kind of content that drills deep into the soul of a viewer and stays there."
A long silence followed her words.
No one said anything for a good bit.
Then Luna whispered, voicing her realization.
"... You want our adult content to solely focus on Kai instead of all of us."
Her voice wasn’t angry, but it wasn’t without weight. There was understanding there... and tension beneath it.
Aria added her own words with a pale face: "You no longer want to appeal to the male viewers."
Nyx didn’t deny it.
She nodded once.

"Look, even if our views and income got halved by losing every single male viewer overnight—which wouldn’t even be half since we’ve already established that the desperate chicks are more willing to pay for the ultimate fantasy of watching Kai with first POV and better resolution than a manmade camera could ever provide—we’d still be more than over the requirement to reach rank 3. Based on the numbers the system has put forth thus far, the female fans are enough. We’ll just need to rope many of them in."
Luna’s whisper came next.
