"Anyways...
Let’s shift focus."
The girls laughed together at him running away, but didn’t press the matter any further.
A flicker of light shimmered into being above his palm.
The System window returned.
[New System Quest: Fangirl Bottleneck]
"This is what we’re dealing with now," Kaiden said.
"The system’s calling it a bottleneck..." Luna mused, stroking her chin in thought.
"Well, I mean, it clearly is a bottleneck.
There’s no reason to put it more gently," Nyx added.
"We have more than three times the needed views and income to reach rank 3, but we’re only one-tenth of the way to reach the fangirl requirement."
"But what else can we do?" Aria asked before continuing,
"Based on its own wording, which was ’the Successor must cultivate a following whose devotion stems from genuine connection and profound inspiration.

Superficial engagement, while boosting views and income, does not translate into the deep admiration required for this metric.’ It clearly suggests that the fangirl metric is simply going to be slower to accumulate than the other two, no matter what we do."
Luna nodded in agreement.
"You’re right, I believe.
And we’ve already been trying to make Kai appeal to the horny sluts by doing variety content and also having things like your nurse RP focus on him."
*Clap!*
Nyx clapped her hands once, sharp and loud.
"Okay!
Hear me out," she murmured with excited eyes.
"Instead of taking this side quest as us assuming that the system is saying we’re doing horribly... maybe we should take it as the system saying we’re just not doing enough."
Kaiden raised a brow.
"Not enough?"
Nyx nodded.
"Exactly!
We’ve been dipping our toes into things, trying to be versatile, trying a little bit of everything.
But the fangirl metric doesn’t reward ’a little of everything.’ It rewards obsession.
We need to lean in, hard.
Stop playing it safe and greedy."
Kaiden was a bit skeptical as he asked, "What do you suggest we do, then?"
Nyx leaned back in her chair, tapping a finger against her lips in exaggerated thought.
Silence hung for a beat.
Then her lips curled into a grin.
Slow, confident, and utterly devilish.
"We need to rebrand."
"...Rebrand?" Aria asked, confused.
Luna didn’t speak.
She just narrowed her eyes, her amusement gone, replaced with focused scrutiny.
She knew Nyx well enough to recognize when her gears were turning fast.
Bastet remained silent but watchful.
She didn’t know enough about human entertainment strategy to add to the conversation in any meaningful way for now, but she was clearly intrigued.
After all, her master’s future growth potential was the topic being discussed before her.
Nyx nodded, "Rebrand, yes."
Her eyes were sharp now, the usual mischief replaced by genuine strategy.
"Think back to that night at the sushi place.
When Kaiden made us his Valkyries after the porn shoot."
Her gaze swept across the room, catching the gazes of the other two Valkyries.
"He told us his vision.
That we were going to storm the world with content so bold, so captivating, so insane that no one would be able to ignore it.
That we’d rise to the very top, not just in numbers, not just in influence, but in legacy.
He wanted our faces etched into the damn mythos of this post-apocalypse world."
"And that’s perhaps just a tiny bit too ambitious.
At least, for now.
What we’re seeing now—what this bottleneck quest is telling us—is that there’s a consequence to trying to appeal to everyone at once."
Kaiden furrowed his brow, listening to his girlfriend intently.
"We’re spreading ourselves too thin," Nyx continued.
"We’ve been trying to do it all.
Cater to every fantasy, every viewer type, every demographic.
Some content for women, some for men, some for the lonely, the horny, the curious, the bloodthirsty.
And it’s worked.
We dominate in views and income."
She lifted a finger.
"But that third metric?
That devotion?
It doesn’t care how wide we cast the net.
It only cares about depth.
About emotional entanglement.
About fixation."
The air in the room shifted as her words sank in.
"So here’s what I’m proposing.
We stop worrying about appealing to everyone on Planet Earth.
We accept a drop in views and income.
We narrow our focus.
We build something targeted.
Intimate.
The kind of content that drills deep into the soul of a viewer and stays there."
A long silence followed her words.
No one said anything for a good bit.
Then Luna whispered, voicing her realization.
You want our adult content to solely focus on Kai instead of all of us."
Her voice wasn’t angry, but it wasn’t without weight.
There was understanding there... and tension beneath it.
Aria added her own words with a pale face: "You no longer want to appeal to the male viewers."
Nyx didn’t deny it.
She nodded once.

"Look, even if our views and income got halved by losing every single male viewer overnight—which wouldn’t even be half since we’ve already established that the desperate chicks are more willing to pay for the ultimate fantasy of watching Kai with first POV and better resolution than a manmade camera could ever provide—we’d still be more than over the requirement to reach rank 3.
Based on the numbers the system has put forth thus far, the female fans are enough.
We’ll just need to rope many of them in."
Luna’s whisper came next.

chapters.title: Chapter 199: Change of Plans
paragraphs: "And it’d also help with our image... Kaiden wouldn’t be called a cuck by the insecure ones, and our bodies wouldn’t be plastered all over the internet either."
She paused, folding her arms under her chest, eyes narrowed in thought.

"Think about it... Right now, half the commentary around us comes from bitter assholes online calling Kaiden a ’manager’ instead of the main act. They see us getting railed on camera and assume he’s just the cameraman with benefits. They’re not seeing him as the center: he’s being drowned out by the spectacle of us."
She shifted, tapping a finger against her forearm, letting the thought hang before driving it home.

"That’s a problem. Especially if we’re serious about building a devoted female following. If we delete the content that focuses on us, we do more than just clean up the narrative. We reinforce something very, very important. That our attention, our desire, our bodies—they’re not public property. They’re not for casual consumption. They’re for him. For the Blood Knight, the Paragon of Sin, the man of every woman’s dreams."
She glanced at Aria, Bastet, Nyx, and then back at Kaiden.
"And that exclusivity matters. A lot."

"Female viewers love obsession. Intensity. They fantasize about being chosen. And if they’re seeing Kaiden as this turbo-competent, ultra-handsome, immensely powerful guy that is surrounded by beautiful women who don’t sell their sex tapes to random guys for money and fame but instead just orbit their chosen man like he’s their sun? That’s magnetic."
She gave a sharp nod to herself.

"Suddenly, there’s no more of the ’cuck’ narrative. There’s no more ’pimp’ angle. No more ’open harem porn troupe’ commentary from the peanut gallery. Instead, there’s mystery. Respect. The idea that he’s the prize. That he’s not some desperate dude monetizing his girls, but someone who keeps his private life private unless it means something."

"And the women watching?" she finished, leaning back in her chair with a satisfied smile. "They’re gonna want to be that girl. The one who breaks through. Who’s not just a viewer, but his fangirl. His chosen."
Suddenly, Luna’s eyes narrowed as she glanced over at Nyx, surprise visible in her eyes.

Then, with zero warning and using her high Agility stat, she reached across and delivered a resounding slap to Nyx’s chest, a full, open-palm smack that made a distinct whap sound against her massive breasts, making them jiggle violently even while being restrained by her bras.
Nyx jolted, letting out a yelp. "Hey!"
Luna smirked, not feeling apologetic one bit. "I didn’t know you had actual thoughts behind those watermelons... I’m honestly impressed. That was a good idea."
Nyx blinked, holding her boobs protectively to stop their jiggling. "Was that really necessary, Bestie?"
Luna ignored the protest. "I take back what I said last week. Maybe you’re more than just a pair of tits good enough to bait simps into watching us."
Nyx narrowed her eyes, though a grin crept up the side of her mouth.

"Well..." she mused, tilting her head as that signature smug grin of hers curved across her lips. "I guess it takes more than tits to mastermind a rebrand. But hey, it doesn’t hurt to have both an amazing brain and overwhelming feminine appeal. Makes me feel like a dual wielder."
"..." Kaiden didn’t even get a chance to groan before Luna’s expression shifted sharply.
Her amusement evaporated. Frost crept into her eyes.

"Okay, I see what you’re saying, Nyx," Aria cut in before another slapfest broke out. Her voice was steady, thoughtful. her default mode when faced with high-stakes decisions. "We can achieve many benefits by focusing on female viewers only. I’m in."
But then, her smile thinned.
Soured.
Her eyes narrowed, flicking over to Kaiden.
"...But what about the content we’ve already uploaded? The stuff that focuses on us instead of Kai?"
It was a good question. But instead of panicking, Luna and Nyx exchanged a brief glance.
Smug. Confident.
They knew.
"Most of our stuff," Luna began, "is exclusively hosted on the Awakened Media Platform. There, we have complete control. No downloads. No rips. No third-party mirrors."
Nyx continued smoothly. "It’s better than any human-made content platform could ever hope to become and is more secure to boot. So, if we delete something?"
She gave a theatrical shrug, her smirk widening.
"It’s gone. Wiped. Zero chance of it getting out."
"But..." Kaiden ventured.
"Yeah," Nyx nodded, expression turning grim. "There’s a but. A rather big but..."
"The Zadie shoot," Luna finished with a sigh. "The initial one. Our debut with that horribly disgustingly named Untainted Holes studio..."

Nyx nodded. "That one was different. It went public on multiple sites, using the internet, not the Awakened Platform. Free and paid. Clipped. Compiled. Pirated. If it isn’t already floating around the net in five languages and ten formats, it will be."
Aria sighed with a wry expression. "So we’re already compromised."

"Not yet," Luna decreed sharply. "It might not have blown up yet. We have a narrow window. The Bastet Subjugation video was what put us in the spotlight, and that video was posted less than a day ago. Our other Awakened Platform content should keep those who want to dig into us occupied, giving us a bit more time to erase the internet content before they run out of our awakened videos and start looking elsewhere."

Aria’s eyes glinted as she got on the same wavelength as her friends. "Then we need to move! Fast. We either bury it in the next few hours before it spreads more than it already has, or the plan we just made is nothing but a useless dream."
[Ding!]
A sharp ding echoed in Kaiden’s mind all of a sudden.
His thoughts halted.
Without needing to will it, a shimmer of light flickered above his palm. The familiar glow of a System Message manifested.
Everyone went quiet as Kaiden brought the window up.
It read:
[New Quest: Burn the Bridges]
Classification: Time-Limited Emergency Protocol
Trigger: Public Compromise of Core Image Strategy
[Description:]
The Demonic Pornstar System acknowledges the strategic shift enacted by the Successor and his Valkyries.

The pursuit of a fangirl-centric following, built upon emotional obsession and exclusive intimacy, aligns with the System’s core philosophy. Both the Demonic Pornstar System and the Heavenly Demon recognize this as a high-sin, high-return path.
But before this path can be paved...
The past must be purged.
[Objective:]
Permanently eliminate the Untainted Holes adult studio content across the open internet. Ensure no remaining files exist on mainstream platforms and company storage.
[Constraints:]
• Time Limit: 4 Hours
• Must avoid triggering wider attention or scandals during the removal process.
[Success Reward:] The System will deploy [Abyssal Redaction], permanently erasing residual data from all non-system-integrated storage, including civilian downloads, caches, and pirated vaults.
[Recommended Actions: Mobilize. Delegate. Infiltrate. Bribe. Threaten. Silence. Whatever it takes.]
[You’ve chosen your truth. Now burn the lie.]
Kaiden stared at the rather long quest prompt for a few seconds. The countdown ticked in the corner.
He didn’t need to say anything.
The room filled with a quiet intensity.
This wasn’t just a rebrand anymore.
It was war.
And it had already started.

chapters.title: Chapter 200: Great Boon
paragraphs: The round table at the top of XXXVidz Tower was lit up by artificial lights, a projection of prestige and power. The windowless chamber—deep within the corporate district’s core—was where deals were made, destinies altered, and reputations sold.

Zadie sat straight-backed at the far end, legs crossed, coffee untouched. Her gaze was fixed on the central display, currently playing four looping thumbnails: Kaiden. Aria. Luna. Nyx. A highlight reel from their debut shoot. The watermark read Untainted Holes, but the overlay screamed something else.
VALHALLA’S SINNERS — UNCUT. UNHOLY. UNFORGETTABLE.
Across from her, Executive Marlow, a bloated man who wheezed even while sitting, jiggled as he laughed.
"We’ve got a goldmine and it’s just sitting there behind a damned niche studio paywall!"

He slapped his belly for whatever reason before he continued. "I say we run a proper ad campaign to push it on the socials, maybe even get the edgy influencers to plug it, and our revenue’s gonna break company records tenfold. Hell, I’m talking quarter-shifting returns! Our stockholders are going to drool while screaming our praises!"

Vesta, her expensive jewelry items clinking one after the other as she stirred her drink without sipping, spoke up. Her voice was smooth but carried the cold indifference of a woman used to stepping on necks.

"This could finally be our chance to move beyond the decaying corpse that is the old web. Let the traditionalists rot. The Awakened Media Platform is where everything’s heading. Money, attention, influence. If we move fast, we could carve a serious piece out of the awakened porn pie. Maybe even challenge ChronosX if we play our cards right."
Zadie’s lips parted.
"We should consider reaching out to Valhalla’s Sinners for their go-ahead."
There was a pause around the round table. Then a snort.
Renzo, eyes permanently narrowed like a lizard in human skin, waved her off.
"Oh, don’t be stupid, Zadie. We own those videos. They signed the release under your watch. What Kaiden and his sluts want doesn’t matter one bit; we can do whatever the hell we want."
Zadie’s eyes darkened. Her pupils narrowed to slits.

"I’m well aware of the legality being entirely on our side, Renzo. I just think it’s not smart to provoke a group that’s rising faster than any content creators we’ve ever seen. Especially not ones that can not only bring in unseen numbers but also rapidly grow as awakened combatants. If they see this as a betrayal, we won’t be fighting lawsuits, but angry awakened people who are after our necks. It’s smarter to get their go-ahead."

"Pfft." Delia Krome, arms draped over the back of her chair, rolled her eyes. "You’ve gone soft, Zadie. Where’s the old monster I know? Maybe you still feel sentimental ’cause you cast them for that shoot. What, seeing that handsome pecker up close make you blush?"
The others broke into chuckles at that, amusement dripping with mockery. For a high-ranking executive like Zadie to have stepped in as caster was unorthodox. It was, in their eyes, a demotion.
Zadie didn’t rise to the bait. Her fingers only tapped the table once. Cold. Controlled.
But she didn’t get to make her comeback because the room suddenly stilled when the door hissed open and a junior assistant burst in, out of breath, tablet clutched to her chest,
"I-I apologize for the interruption!"
Renzo growled, "We said no interruptions."
"Yes, I know, but... Kaiden is here. He’s requesting a private meeting with all executives."
Vesta blinked, straightening her spine. "You mean that Kaiden?"
The assistant nodded grimly.
Zadie’s gaze sharpened. "Did he say what he’s hoping to achieve by coming to us?"
"No. Just that it was for ’executive ears only.’"
For the first time since the meeting began, the smug amusement in the room drained. Replaced by quiet, electrified tension.
Zadie nodded, accepting the assistant’s words.
"Then let’s not keep him waiting."
The conference doors creaked open.
In stepped Kaiden.

No fanfare. No dramatic poses. Just a slow, deliberate gait that turned the oxygen in the room into something heavier, thicker. A lead blanket of sheer presence that dragged every executive’s eyes to him like magnets drawn to steel.
He wore civilian clothes. A plain black hoodie and dark jeans, no brand logos, no awakened gear. But it didn’t matter. His eyes said more than any uniform ever could.

They were hollow, sharp, and alert. Not dead, but something worse: aware. Alert in a way that said he knew every line of sight in this room. That if things went wrong, he’d pick who to maim first based on efficiency. Not emotion.
A shiver passed through Zadie before she could stop it.
’This...’ she thought, her mouth suddenly turning dry. ’This is the same boy I cast less than a week ago? The awkward, wide-eyed cutie here to screw some pretty girls on camera and get paid for it?’

The man standing before her now... this wasn’t someone looking to impress. This was someone who came with a purpose, and the implicit threat that anyone who denied him that purpose would regret it deeply.
He stopped at the table.
"Hope I’m not interrupting."
His voice was quiet. Controlled. But it landed with the same weight as if it were a weapon placed gently on the table: Seen, not used. Yet.
Behind him followed three distinct auras. Not bodyguards. Not decorations. Just power walking in three separate flavors.
Aria. Silver hair flowing, eyes dull but sharp. A blade still sheathed but ready. She looked around the room with badly veiled disgust like someone scanning a menu she had no appetite for.

Nyx was next, hands in her coat pockets, chewing faintly on a pink lollipop with a blank look in her eyes. Her aura was spacey, aloof. But something about the way her pupils occasionally flicked to the execs was... measuring. As if assessing which one of them would break first if she pushed.

Luna came last. Her face wore mild annoyance, lips pressed in a line. Not angry, not rude... just looking as if this whole meeting was a waste of time. Like she’d rather be training. Or sleeping. Or killing something.
Together, the four didn’t look like a content creator and his cast.
They looked like a problem.
None of them smiled. None of them offered greetings.
Marlow began to frown strongly. Delia Krome lost her smirk. Even Vesta’s fingers twitched against her cocktail glass. Renzo scowled, trying to sit taller in his chair.
Zadie eyed them for a bit longer, and in that silence, she was the only one who managed to say something.
"Kaiden. Luna. Aria. Nyx. To what do we owe the pleasure?"
Kaiden’s eyes flicked from face to face. Evaluating. Judging.
Then, at last, he spoke.
"You have something that I want. Why else would I come to a place like this?"
Zadie exhaled slowly. She already knew where this was going.
"You want the videos."
It wasn’t a question. It didn’t need to be.
Even without knowing the exact circumstances behind Kaiden’s storm-cloud entrance and the way his Valkyries loomed like bored executioners at his back, it wasn’t hard to put the pieces together.

They’d only ever uploaded their content to the Awakened Media Platform—a controlled space. Locked down. No copies, no piracy, no risk. Every frame monitored, every view counted, every ounce of power held firmly in their hands.
And then there were ’those’ videos. The debut trilogy. Untainted Holes’ crown jewels. Freely floating around the festering remnants of the old internet, outside their control.
Zadie’s lips twisted. "If it were me in your position, I’d want the same."
Before she could say more, Marlow suddenly exploded.
"Absolutely not!"

"You’ve gone soft, Zadie.
Where’s the old monster I know?
Maybe you still feel sentimental ’cause you cast them for that shoot.
What, seeing that handsome pecker up close make you blush?"
The others broke into chuckles at that, amusement dripping with mockery.
For a high-ranking executive like Zadie to have stepped in as caster was unorthodox.
It was, in their eyes, a demotion.
Zadie didn’t rise to the bait.
Her fingers only tapped the table once.
Cold.
Controlled.
But she didn’t get to make her comeback because the room suddenly stilled when the door hissed open and a junior assistant burst in, out of breath, tablet clutched to her chest,
"I-I apologize for the interruption!"
Renzo growled, "We said no interruptions."
"Yes, I know, but...
Kaiden is here.
He’s requesting a private meeting with all executives."
Vesta blinked, straightening her spine.
"You mean that Kaiden?"
The assistant nodded grimly.
Zadie’s gaze sharpened.
"Did he say what he’s hoping to achieve by coming to us?"
"No.
Just that it was for ’executive ears only.’"
For the first time since the meeting began, the smug amusement in the room drained.
Replaced by quiet, electrified tension.
Zadie nodded, accepting the assistant’s words.
"Then let’s not keep him waiting."
The conference doors creaked open.
In stepped Kaiden.
No fanfare.
No dramatic poses.
Just a slow, deliberate gait that turned the oxygen in the room into something heavier, thicker.
A lead blanket of sheer presence that dragged every executive’s eyes to him like magnets drawn to steel.
He wore civilian clothes.
A plain black hoodie and dark jeans, no brand logos, no awakened gear.
But it didn’t matter.
His eyes said more than any uniform ever could.
They were hollow, sharp, and alert.
Not dead, but something worse: aware.
Alert in a way that said he knew every line of sight in this room.
That if things went wrong, he’d pick who to maim first based on efficiency.
Not emotion.
A shiver passed through Zadie before she could stop it.
’This...’ she thought, her mouth suddenly turning dry. ’This is the same boy I cast less than a week ago?
The awkward, wide-eyed cutie here to screw some pretty girls on camera and get paid for it?’
The man standing before her now... this wasn’t someone looking to impress.
This was someone who came with a purpose, and the implicit threat that anyone who denied him that purpose would regret it deeply.
He stopped at the table.
"Hope I’m not interrupting."
His voice was quiet.
Controlled.
But it landed with the same weight as if it were a weapon placed gently on the table: Seen, not used.
Yet.
Behind him followed three distinct auras.
Not bodyguards.
Not decorations.
Just power walking in three separate flavors.
Aria.
Silver hair flowing, eyes dull but sharp.
A blade still sheathed but ready.
She looked around the room with badly veiled disgust like someone scanning a menu she had no appetite for.
Nyx was next, hands in her coat pockets, chewing faintly on a pink lollipop with a blank look in her eyes.
Her aura was spacey, aloof.
But something about the way her pupils occasionally flicked to the execs was... measuring.
As if assessing which one of them would break first if she pushed.
Luna came last.
Her face wore mild annoyance, lips pressed in a line.
Not angry, not rude... just looking as if this whole meeting was a waste of time.
Like she’d rather be training.
Or sleeping.
Or killing something.
Together, the four didn’t look like a content creator and his cast.
They looked like a problem.
None of them smiled.
None of them offered greetings.
Marlow began to frown strongly.
Delia Krome lost her smirk.
Even Vesta’s fingers twitched against her cocktail glass.
Renzo scowled, trying to sit taller in his chair.
Zadie eyed them for a bit longer, and in that silence, she was the only one who managed to say something.
"Kaiden.
Luna.
Aria.
Nyx.
To what do we owe the pleasure?"
Kaiden’s eyes flicked from face to face.
Evaluating.
Judging.
Then, at last, he spoke.
"You have something that I want.
Why else would I come to a place like this?"
Zadie exhaled slowly.
She already knew where this was going.
"You want the videos."
It wasn’t a question.
It didn’t need to be.
Even without knowing the exact circumstances behind Kaiden’s storm-cloud entrance and the way his Valkyries loomed like bored executioners at his back, it wasn’t hard to put the pieces together.
They’d only ever uploaded their content to the Awakened Media Platform—a controlled space.
Locked down.
No copies, no piracy, no risk.
Every frame monitored, every view counted, every ounce of power held firmly in their hands.
And then there were ’those’ videos.
The debut trilogy.
Untainted Holes’ crown jewels.
Freely floating around the festering remnants of the old internet, outside their control.
Zadie’s lips twisted.
"If it were me in your position, I’d want the same."
Before she could say more, Marlow suddenly exploded.
"Absolutely not!"
